answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain custody of 1,000 unique data shards to verify active storage. A verifier requests unpredictable file segments, which agents must return within a set timeframe. An honest agent incurs a baseline disk cost, whereas 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost by maintaining independent files. This process acts like a canyon where only distinct shards survive, checked by a raven protocol that audits every access. Should any agent fail to prove retrieval, the tide of audits will result in an immediate slash of their deposit, ensuring no refunds for collusion.
